items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: a drummer was named Sonny Greer; they were all out of St. Louis. Swinging little cats. And I mean they were older than I was. I was just, like I said, just a teenager.

ctx.x: Martha Davis, yeah. An alto player came through there out of St. Louis named Burt Brazier. Now Burt come through Chicago with a pianist -- only had one leg, Greer? and a drummer was named Sonny Greer; they were all out of St. Louis. Swinging little cats. And I mean they were older than I was. I was just, like I said, just a teenager. And they were playing, oh, to me -- Burt was sounding like Benny Carter would sound, you know, on alto. But he didn't know the music. I didn't find this out until later, because I…

the WPA band -- he was in the WPA band. He remembered me. And I said, 'Burt?' And he said, 'Bubble ...' -- he used to call everybody 'Bubble Kitchen'. He said, 'Bubble Kitchen, I never learned how to read music. I can hardly play it unless it's written out.' And I took that advice and I figured if I learned how to read, I would lose all my natural ability.
